warn.edit:
Tech preview: OCR Lite does not keep your edits yet — a crash or a reload loses the text on the right. Copy or save what you change.

Real editing, with the work kept, is the next major step.
set.lang.hint: Follows the browser's language unless chosen here; kept in this browser.
set.expert.hint: Shows the decoding presets and technical details (model files, GPU memory); kept in this browser. Off: every read uses the default preset.

about.hint: Reads historic handwriting with a LightOnOCR model fine-tuned for this project. Everything runs on this device; images never leave it.
su.where.p1: OCR Lite reads on this device. It needs the model (1.4 GB, downloaded once from Hugging Face) in the browser's storage.
su.where.p2: An installed app (Home Screen, Dock, Chrome / Edge app) has its own storage, apart from this tab — so download the model inside the app you will use.
su.ready: Ready — open an image and press Read.
su.ready.hint: Opening an image puts Auto's rectangle around the writing — adjust it, then ✓; Contrast or Pencil help with faint ink or uneven paper.
su.installed: Installed — open OCR Lite from your apps and continue the setup there; this tab can be closed.
su.haveModel: The model is already in this browser's storage.
su.modelNote: The model — {name} — (1.4 GB) is downloaded once from {from} into this browser's storage; later visits read it from there, offline too.
su.noRoom: This browser offers only {free} of storage for this site — the model needs {need}. Free space on the device, then download.
su.cancelled: Download cancelled — the model is not stored.
su.inst.ios.title: iPhone / iPad · Safari
su.inst.ios.1: Tap {icon} next to the address bar.
su.inst.ios.3: Scroll down and tap “Add to Home Screen”.
su.inst.ios.4: Leave “Open as Web App” on, then tap “Add”.
su.inst.ios.5: Open OCR Lite from the Home Screen.
su.inst.ios.note: With the tab layout “Top” or “Bottom”, Share {icon} sits right in the toolbar: tap it and go on with step 3.
su.inst.iosByHand: On iPhone and iPad OCR Lite is added by hand — Apple does not allow a direct install button.
su.inst.mac-safari.title: Mac · Safari
su.inst.mac-safari.1: Click Share {icon} in the toolbar (or open the File menu).
su.inst.mac-safari.4: Open OCR Lite from the Dock.
su.inst.chrome.bar.1: Click {icon} at the right end of the address bar (left of the star).
su.inst.chrome.bar.3: Open OCR Lite from your apps.
su.inst.edge.bar.1: Click the “App available” icon {icon} in the address bar.
su.inst.edge.bar.3: Open OCR Lite from your apps.
su.inst.ifNoChip: If it is not there — install from the menu:
su.inst.chrome.title: Chrome · computer
su.inst.chrome.1: Open the menu {icon} at the top right.
su.inst.edge.title: Edge · computer
su.inst.edge.1: Open “Settings and more” {icon} at the top right.
su.inst.edge.3: Choose “Install this site as an app”.
su.inst.android-chrome.title: Android · Chrome
su.inst.android-chrome.1: Open the menu {icon} at the top right.
su.inst.android-chrome.2: Choose “Add to Home screen” or “Install app”.
su.inst.android-chrome.4: Open OCR Lite from the Home screen.
su.inst.android-edge.title: Android · Edge
su.inst.android-edge.1: Open the menu {icon} at the bottom.
su.inst.android-edge.4: Open OCR Lite from the Home screen.

su.inst.other.title: Other browsers
su.inst.other.text: No app install known for this browser — OCR Lite runs in this tab.
su.inst.ifNoButton: If the button does not appear — install from the menu:

upd.busy: A read is running — reload when it is done
upd.confirm: Reload now? The text on the right is not saved.
h.noWebGpu: OCR Lite needs WebGPU — this browser has none (Chrome / Edge 113+, Safari 26+; on Linux Chrome: enable it in chrome://flags)
h.crashMem:
This device does not have enough memory for OCR Lite: the device check's memory test ({when}) needed {gb} GB of GPU memory and the system ended the app.

OCR Lite runs on Macs and iPads with Apple silicon and on recent iPhones (experimental). You can still try — the next read tries again.
h.crashKilled: OCR Lite stopped during {step} ({when}) — most likely this device ran out of memory.
h.crashLost: OCR Lite lost the GPU during {step} ({when}): {why}.
h.cleared: Device notice cleared — Read tries again
h.lastKilled: The last run stopped during {step} without finishing ({when}, build {build}) — most likely this device ran out of memory.
h.lastLost: The last run lost the GPU during {step} ({when}): {why}.
h.needGpu: {what} OCR Lite needs {need} of GPU memory (an iPad / Mac with Apple silicon, or a desktop GPU).
h.nextDevice: {why} — the next read starts on a new GPU device
h.readEnds: {why} — the read ends; the next one starts on a new GPU device
h.foreign: The model in this browser did not come from {from} and is not used
h.noModel: No model in this browser yet
h.formatLater: weights / compute: shown once the model is loaded (first read)
h.mem.pool: GPU memory held by the engine: {mb} (its memory pool, kept from read to read; each read loads its weights into it)
h.mem.idle: GPU memory: {mb} before the first read
h.mem.last: last read: weights {weights} · peak {peak} (in its {phase}) · load {s} s
h.mem.afterFirst: weights + peak: shown after the first read
h.mem.later: GPU memory: shown once the model is loaded — a full page needs {need}
h.evict: the browser may evict it under storage pressure
h.notUsed: · not used: only a model downloaded from {from} reads — download it
h.verifyOk: The stored model is intact: version {version} (both files match the release).
h.verifyBad1: The stored model is damaged: {files} differs from the release. Delete the model (Settings) and download it again.
h.verifyBadN: The stored model is damaged: {files} differ from the release. Delete the model (Settings) and download it again.
h.verifyUnknown: The stored model matches no released version — delete it and download it again.
h.uploadOff: uploading model files is switched off — download the model from {from}
h.urlOff: {url}: downloading from another folder is switched off — the model comes from {from}
h.enterUrl: enter the URL of a folder holding both model files
h.testHint: A test build: the model is downloaded once from this server ({path}), then read from this browser's storage, offline too — a copy of the open model (CC BY-SA 4.0) from its

preset.head: Decoding presets
preset.hint: Shipped presets (presets.json) are read-only — duplicate one to make your own.
preset.readonly: a shipped preset is read-only — Duplicate makes an editable copy
h.checkAgain: Checking this device's GPU again (the first run is often cold)…
h.memTestOk: Memory test passed: {gb} GB of GPU memory written and held (what a read of the largest page uses) in {s} s.
g.squareNote: This GPU binds at most {have} per buffer — enough for portrait pages; a full-size square image needs {need}: crop it first.
g.insecure.title: Not a secure page
g.insecure: WebGPU only runs on HTTPS (or localhost). Open OCR Lite by its https:// address.
g.safari.update: Safari has WebGPU from version 26. Update {where}, then open OCR Lite again.
g.safari.engine: Every browser on iPad / iPhone uses Safari's engine — the update is the way.
g.safari.offMac: WebGPU is switched off in this Safari: Safari → Settings → Advanced → Show features for web developers, then Feature Flags → WebGPU on. Or use Chrome / Edge.
g.safari.offIos: WebGPU is switched off: Settings → Apps → Safari → Advanced → Feature Flags → WebGPU on.
g.firefox: WebGPU is not available in this Firefox. Use Chrome, Edge or Safari 26+.
g.chrome.update: {label} has WebGPU from version 113: update {label} (menu → Help → About), then reload.
g.linux.title: {label} on Linux
g.linux: WebGPU is still off by default on Linux: open {flags}, enable "Unsafe WebGPU Support" (#enable-unsafe-webgpu) and "Vulkan" (#enable-vulkan), restart {label}.
g.android.title: {label} on Android
g.android: WebGPU needs Android 12 or later and a supported GPU; update Chrome. A phone is unlikely to have the GPU memory OCR Lite needs.
g.blocked: WebGPU is blocked here — most likely for this graphics driver. Update the graphics driver; {page} says why WebGPU is off.
g.other.title: This browser
g.other: It has no WebGPU. Use Chrome or Edge 113+, or Safari 26+.
g.win.title: Windows: the graphics card for the browser
g.win: If this computer also has an NVIDIA / AMD graphics card: Settings → System → Display → Graphics → add the browser (chrome.exe / msedge.exe) → Options → High performance. Then quit the browser completely (all windows, and the tray icon) and start it again.
g.nv.title: NVIDIA Control Panel
g.nv: Manage 3D settings → Program settings → the browser → Preferred graphics processor: High-performance NVIDIA processor.
g.power.title: Power
g.power: Keep the laptop on mains power — on battery the fast GPU is often held back or switched off.
g.linuxGpu.title: Linux: the discrete GPU
g.linuxGpu: Start the browser on the discrete GPU with PRIME offload: DRI_PRIME=1 google-chrome (Mesa), or prime-run google-chrome (NVIDIA); keep the laptop on mains power.
g.intelMac.title: Intel Mac with two GPUs
g.intelMac: System Settings → Battery → Options → turn off "Automatic graphics switching" (older macOS: Energy Saver), then restart the browser; keep it on mains power.
g.iphone: iPhone: experimental — tested on an iPhone 16 Pro (43 tokens/s). The memory test checks this iPhone; older iPhones may not have enough memory. An iPad or a Mac with Apple silicon is fine.
g.noWebGpu: This browser has no WebGPU — OCR Lite cannot run here.
g.failed: The GPU check failed — OCR Lite cannot run here.
g.noAdapter: No usable GPU — the browser offers WebGPU but no graphics adapter.
g.driver.title: Graphics driver
g.driver: Update the graphics driver and the browser. Chrome / Edge: chrome://gpu (edge://gpu) says why WebGPU has no adapter. A remote desktop or a virtual machine often has no GPU.
g.software: Only software rendering (no GPU acceleration) — far too slow for OCR Lite.
g.accel.title: Hardware acceleration
g.accel: Turn on "Use graphics acceleration when available" (Chrome / Edge: Settings → System), update the graphics driver, restart the browser.
g.limits: This GPU cannot run OCR Lite: {names} too small.
g.limit: {name}: this GPU allows {have}, OCR Lite needs {need}
g.f32: No shader-f16 on this GPU: OCR Lite runs its f32 path — it works, but slower and with more GPU memory.
g.f32wg: f32 path (this GPU's workgroup memory is too small for f16): slower, more memory.
g.iphoneOom: This iPhone ran out of memory in an earlier read.
g.speed: Speed: est. {est} tokens/s (memory {gbps} GB/s · {us} µs per dispatch; the M3 reads ≈ {ref})
g.ok: This device can run OCR Lite (GPU: {gpu}, est. {est} tokens/s).
g.integratedOk: This looks like the built-in (integrated) GPU. If the computer also has a graphics card, the browser may run faster on it:
g.slow: OCR Lite will be slow here: est. {est} tokens/s (a page of 900 tokens ≈ {s} s; on an M3 Mac ≈ 11 s).
g.verySlow: OCR Lite will be very slow here: est. {est} tokens/s (a page of 900 tokens ≈ {min} min).
g.integratedSlow: The browser seems to use the built-in (integrated) GPU. If this computer has a graphics card too:
